Democrats will control the House and Senate in the new year, and they have a long list of priorities ahead of them. But it remains to be seen just how much they will focus on one of the most pressing issues of our times: the climate crisis. The UN declared this summer that, despite some progress, it is now “unavoidable” that the globe will heat past the point that scientists say will threaten human health. items.title: The Guardian view on press freedom: authoritarians target journalism because it matters | Editorial
items.summary:
From Cairo to Moscow to Washington, governments are turning up the pressure on media workers

Lina Attalah is an influential Egyptian journalist. Yet until last month, even she was unaware of a major and concerning piece of news: her own conviction. In 2024, a court issued her a one-year sentence for “spreading false news” and running a website without a licence – which she had repeatedly sought to obtain – after trying her in absentia, even though she was in the country. Ms Attalah learned of the case only after she was separately tried in October, resulting in a large fine and an order for the closure of the Mada Masr website. She faces retrial later this month.

Meanwhile, the entire newsroom of the fact-checking website Matsadash remain in detention weeks after authorities snatched the six journalists on charges including joining and financing a terrorist group and spreading false news. Their lawyers say that they have been tortured and forced to record fabricated confessions.

Continue reading...
items.t: The Guardian view on press freedom: authoritarians target journalism because it matters | Editorial

items.title: Mom who plowed into soccer field and killed 2 will not face charges, DA says
items.summary:
A driver who was asleep at the wheel when her pickup truck plowed onto a youth soccer field, killing a young boy and a father, will not face criminal charges following an investigation, prosecutors announced.

Last month, the driver, who has not been identified by authorities, drove into players and spectators at the Stryker Sports Complex in Wichita, Kansas. Cole Adrian, 6, and Nicholas Schafer, 35, were both killed and several others were injured in the Oct. 17 incident.

On Thursday, a 28-page report released by Sedgwick County District Attorney Marc Bennett said investigators did not find enough evidence to charge the driver, concluding the crash was the result of "negligence" rather than a criminal act.

PEOPLE TAKING COMMON SLEEP DRUG MAY NOT REALIZE THEY'RE TOO IMPAIRED TO DRIVE, STUDY FINDS

"The reasonable conclusion is that, while she slept, her foot unintentionally hit the gas pedal while the truck was in gear," the report says. Investigators could not determine exactly how the truck came to be in drive.

items.title: MICHAEL RUIZ: Cold case DNA unmasks 'Montauk Mary' as cops probe link to Jersey Shore 'Thrill Killer'
items.summary:
She survived the Great Depression only to vanish in 1978 and remain an unidentified Jane Doe until nearly a half-century later, when cold case detectives identified her as a possible victim of the Jersey Shore's infamous "Thrill Killer."

Sofia Margherita Marrone had been known for years only as "Montauk Mary" due to where she had been found by a U.S. Airman on his lunch break in a park near the eastern end of Montauk in the town of East Hampton, New York.

On March 22, 1978, the Airman saw Marrone's body near the Camp Hero radar tower that decades later would inspire Netflix's "Stranger Things."

GIRL KNOWN AS 'CHELSEA JANE DOE' ID'D 26 YEARS AFTER MUTILATED BODY FOUND HUNDREDS OF MILES FROM HOME STATE

On Thursday, investigators in Suffolk County identified her as the victim of a shooting 250 miles away from where she had last been seen. They said she had been shot and killed just hours before being found.

Marrone, of Pleasantville, New Jersey, was last seen leaving a hospital in Somers Point, New Jersey, on March 16, 1978. She was killed six days later at East Overlook Park in Montauk. The autopsy found three bullet wounds in her legs and one to her chest.

items.title: New York City building collapse probe raises questions about neighboring property owner’s violation history
items.summary:
The owner of a property next to the site of Wednesday’s deadly building collapse in New York City is facing scrutiny over past construction violations, including a contractor’s decision to defy a city stop-work order in March, according to public records.

Wednesday afternoon's collapse of a three-story building at 1321 Flatbush Ave. in Brooklyn resulted in the deaths of at least eight people and triggered a massive emergency response. The building collapse has raised questions about construction activity next door, where city records show prior violations and a stop-work order that was issued months beforehand.

A stop-work order was issued at the adjacent property, 2621 Bedford Ave., in March by New York City's Department of Buildings, according to public records obtained by Fox News Digital.

The agency determined that the contractors, N Tech Design of America, had failed to install proper safety precautions, which included netting and sheds, Department of Buildings spokesperson Andrew Rudansky told The Gothamist.

items.title: Texas man executed for beheading 3 children: 'Going to be with my kids'
items.summary:
A South Texas man convicted of murdering three young children he helped raise was executed Thursday evening, nearly 23 years after the killings.

John Allen Rubio, 46, of Brownsville, received a lethal injection at a state prison in Huntsville, according to The Associated Press (AP).

Rubio was convicted of stabbing and beheading his children, Julissa Quezada, 3, John Esteban Rubio, 1, and Mary Jane Rubio, 2 months old. He was prosecuted alongside his common-law wife, Angela Camacho.

Rubio was pronounced dead at 6:47 p.m., 21 minutes after the lethal injection began, The AP said. 

OKLAHOMA MAN, 73, EXECUTED FOR PLOTTING MURDER OF LOVER'S HUSBAND, OFFERS NO LAST WORDS

The execution, scheduled for 6 p.m., proceeded without incident.

In his final statement, Rubio thanked his friends and family for their "love and understanding," acknowledged that he was "not the same person I once was" and expressed his love for his wife, according to the AP. 

"I want to say I’m sorry to my wife’s family," he said. "I can’t change the past, but I can tell you my life is going to be over. But that’s not going to make you happy.

"I’m going to be with my kids in a little bit," he added. "I’m ready to go to heaven to be with my lord and savior."
items.t: Texas man executed for beheading 3 children: 'Going to be with my kids'
